t: Ozi gardens the spoke: automation history through work lugs and paired test lugs
description: Replace receipt-first automation history with Ozi-managed spoke history. Every framework or spoke automation change should be enumerated as a durable work lug under an Ozi implementation controller, and each work lug should correspond to one or more paired test lugs. This makes spoke evolution visible, replayable, dogfoodable, and verifiable: Ozi gardens the spoke by turning behavior changes into work, and work into tests.
status_note: Dogfood in this context means refine the implementation lug during this session until it is cold-readable, governance-complete, and ready_to_implement. Naive-agent review findings should be folded back into this lug rather than leaving it in a provisional dogfood state.
problem_statement: Plain receipts in WAI-State.json are useful for replay safety but weak as the authoritative history of framework automation changes. They do not fully capture why a change exists, which Ozi work item created it, how it should be verified, or how later agents should continue it. Canonical Wheelwright needs automation history to live in lugs, with test coverage attached, while WAI-State.json remains minimal runtime truth.

canonical_direction.history_model: Automation history lives in Ozi implementation/work/test lugs, not primarily in opaque state receipts.
canonical_direction.runtime_model: WAI-State.json keeps only minimal runtime and recovery state required for safe execution, replay, and coordination.
canonical_direction.verification_model: Each automation work lug links to one or more test lugs that prove the change.
canonical_direction.operational_model: Ozi is the gardener of spoke evolution: he owns the local implementation controller and orchestrates child work and test lugs inside a spoke.

lug_graph_model.parent_controller: Ozi implementation lug controls a batch or feature area
lug_graph_model.child_work_lugs: Enumerate concrete automation changes with scope, rationale, touched files, and success criteria
lug_graph_model.paired_test_lugs: Each work lug links to one or more verification lugs covering behavior, idempotency, and regression checks
traceability_rules: Every work lug records parent Ozi implementation lug
Every test lug records the work lug(s) it verifies
Every merged automation change can be traced from implementation controller -> work lug -> test lug -> resulting protocol/file updates

initial_target_area.focus: Teaching generation and hub publish flow
sequence: 1. Define child work/test lug schema and linking fields
2. Author child work lugs for teaching generation and hub publish automation
3. Author paired test lugs for idempotency, archive behavior, copy skipping, and wakeup discovery
4. Update closeout policy/spec to reconcile against Ozi-controlled lugs rather than receipt-first history

controller_children.success: changed objects are deterministically grouped into teaching families
exactly one current teaching version exists per family
superseded versions move to archive without deleting distinct history

controller_children.goal: copy current teachings to hub teachings_repo
controller_children.success: hub current/archive state matches local publish state without symlinks
hub indexes reflect current state and survive interrupted writes

controller_children.goal: no-op rerun does not create new version
controller_children.success: unchanged rerun produces no new current or archive artifacts
one current per family and correct archive placement
publish avoids unnecessary recopy and index churn

controller_children.goal: wakeup discovery reads hub indexes without symlink assumptions
controller_children.success: teachings are discoverable from hub index files only

dogfood_requirements.goal: Prove the model is cold-readable and implementable before adopting it as a framework rule.
dogfood_requirements.review_agent: Naive subagent with no framework context beyond the lug text and any directly referenced files
must_validate: The distinction between WAI-State runtime truth and lug-based automation history is clear
A future implementer can tell when to create a work lug vs a test lug vs a runtime state marker
The initial teaching/hub example is sufficient to execute the pattern without chat context
dogfood_requirements.expected_output: STUCK points, ambiguity list, missing schema/field guidance, and any governance gaps

review_questions: Should every Ozi implementation lug require at least one paired test lug before ready_for_recheck?
What is the minimal runtime-only state that still belongs in WAI-State.json after this shift?
How should child work/test lug IDs be named or linked for easy traversal?
Should closeout emit/update work and test lugs directly, or only reconcile state against existing Ozi-controlled lugs?
success_criteria: A dogfooded Ozi-centered pattern exists for automation history
Framework changes are represented as explicit work lugs rather than only state receipts
Work lugs and test lugs form a consistent traceable chain
WAI-State.json role is reduced to runtime truth and recovery markers, not primary historical narrative

dogfood_result.goal: Improve this implementation lug to ready_to_implement in the current session
dogfood_result.definition: Dogfood = tighten scope, remove ambiguity, clarify WAI-State boundaries, and make work/test lug pairing executable by a future builder without chat context
exit_criteria: Cold agent can distinguish Ozi controller lug vs child work lug vs paired test lug
WAI-State.json role is bounded to runtime/recovery truth only
Initial teaching-generation and hub-publish example is concrete enough to implement
Lug is marked ready_to_implement rather than left in dogfood state

creation_rules.controller_lug: Create an Ozi implementation controller for any non-trivial automation batch that spans multiple work items, modifies behavior across files, or needs durable orchestration/history.
creation_rules.work_lug: Create one child work lug per concrete automation change with a distinct success criterion or touched object boundary.
creation_rules.test_lug: Create at least one paired test lug for every work lug before that work lug may advance to ready_for_recheck.
creation_rules.runtime_only_state_marker: Use WAI-State.json only for runtime coordination, recovery, duplicate-detection, locks, active session/runtime mode, and migration/adoption facts required for safe replay.

allowed_in_WAI_State: current runtime pointers such as track_path

before_ready_for_recheck: each child work lug has at least one paired test lug
paired test lugs are at least drafted and linked
runtime-only WAI-State markers are distinguished from historical lugs
before_implemented: paired test lugs executed or ready_for_recheck with evidence
before_accepted: traceability chain controller -> work -> test is intact

closeout_policy.default: Closeout reconciles and updates runtime state plus existing Ozi-controlled lugs; it does not invent new work/test lugs by default.
closeout_policy.exception: Closeout may create narrowly scoped stub lugs only when an explicit Ozi policy authorizes automatic stub creation for a known controller.

fleet_boundary: Octo owns wheel-level scanning and dispatch; Ozi owns local spoke history and execution.

naming_and_linking.controller_to_child: Child lugs must include parent_implementation = ozi-gardens-the-wheel-v1
naming_and_linking.id_convention: Prefer relationship-readable IDs such as work-teaching-family-detection-v1 and test-teaching-family-detection-idempotency-v1

fixes_applied: Added explicit controller/work/test lug field contracts
Added creation rules for controller lugs, child work lugs, test lugs, and runtime-only state markers
Added lifecycle gates tying work lugs to paired test lugs
Added dependency semantics and naming/linking convention
Expanded the initial teaching/hub example into a sequenced mini-spec

alignment_notes: Renamed from wheel gardening to spoke gardening so Octo can own hub-level wheel dispatch.
Canonical implementation record lives in implementation-ozi-gardens-the-spoke-v1; keep this compact lug as design/source material.
